days.title: Protohistoric Settlements and Sacred Waters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Sito di Pianvalle
stops.detail: Of notable interest is the site of Pianvalle, on Monte Croce (via Monte Croce, municipality of Como).

stops.name: Roccia di Pianvalle
stops.detail: Immediately beside the protohistoric settlement, the rock of Pianvalle (a vertical outcrop of gonfolite) has aroused the interest of experts for its notable carvings: cup marks (small semicircular cavities, very common in the Alpine area), spirals, geometric and serpentiform motifs, of uncertain, perhaps ritual or social meaning.

stops.name: Fonte della Mojenca
stops.detail: Remaining in the Municipality of Como, another site of notable interest is the so-called source of Mojenca (whose name could derive from the Celtic words muit or moier, or from the Lombard möi or moia, terms that all indicate a place rich in water).

days.title: Rock-cut Chambers and Military Borders
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Camera Grande
stops.detail: From the Leno locality of the Prestino district, it is possible to reach two large rectangular chambers of the late Bronze Age (10th-9th century BC) carved into the living rock of the hill: the Camera Grande, measuring 8.71 m × 5.05 m, and the smaller Camera Carugo.

stops.name: Camera Carugo
stops.detail: The Camera Grande had residential functions, while for the Camera Carugo it is presumed to have been a room used for metalworking.
